brief.situation: You lead the cloud platform team at Harbor & Pine, a fictional retailer. On the 4th of the month Finance forwards a budget alert: the billing account has spent $4,800 against a $3,000 monthly budget. Nobody knows why. Sales runs its quarterly review at 14:00 on a dashboard the marketing analytics team published last week. It is 09:00.
handover: Each team owns its own projects; your team runs the billing account, the organization policies and the guardrails. Finance sees the bill but not the workloads.
Project mkt-analytics also runs the nightly lead-scoring pipeline.
howItWorks: The board shows the billing account, the project and the people, with what is set up in each; meters show spend.
Each task takes your time: start it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. Spend keeps accruing on the same clock.
When you close the case, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: how you found where the money went, who owns fixing it and why, and what stops the next surprise.

parts.label: Where it went
parts.criteria: Uses Cloud Billing reports (by project, service, SKU) and the job history to trace the increase to one dashboard's full-table queries.
parts.modelAnswer: Billing reports put 92% of the increase in mkt-analytics, BigQuery Analysis, since last Tuesday. The job history showed the new sales dashboard scanning about 2 TiB every 15 minutes because the table is not partitioned.

parts.label: Who owns it
parts.criteria: The project owner is accountable for the workload's cost and fixes it; Finance and the platform team provide visibility and guardrails; blunt shutdowns are avoided.
parts.modelAnswer: Cost is shared: the marketing analytics lead owns the workload and its spend, so their team fixed the query; Finance watches the bill and the platform team sets guardrails. Disabling billing would have stopped the lead-scoring pipeline too and could remove resources.

parts.label: No more surprises
parts.criteria: Explains that an alerts-only budget does not stop spending, and adds a quota, a project budget alerting the owner, required labels and a regular review.
parts.modelAnswer: The existing budget only emailed Finance; it never capped anything. Now a 50 TiB daily query quota stops a runaway, the owner gets the project's budget alerts, every project carries team and owner labels, and spend is reviewed monthly with each owner.

expertPath.text: Billing reports by project, service and SKU; the job history: the sales dashboard scans 2 TiB every 15 minutes.
Find the owner from the project's labels and call them: they own the workload and its cost.
The owner's team partitions the table and refreshes hourly over 7 days; meanwhile set a 50 TiB daily query quota and a project budget alerting the owner.
Required labels on every project and a monthly cost review; the 14:00 review runs on the fixed dashboard.

governed.headline: Good: owned, fixed, guarded
governed.body: You traced the money before acting, put the fix with the team that owns the workload, kept Sales' review safe, and left guardrails that stop the next runaway rather than just email about it.

governedGaps.headline: Stopped, with gaps
governedGaps.body: The runaway is stopped. The criteria show what was late, done around the owner, or left unguarded.

billingOff.headline: Too blunt
billingOff.body: Disabling billing stops every service in the project and can remove resources. A quota, a permission change or the owner's fix stops one query.

reviewFailed.headline: The review had nothing to show
reviewFailed.body: Cutting the dashboard off stopped the spend but also the business it served. Get the owner's fix in before the deadline, or don't cut it.

stillBurning.headline: Still burning
stillBurning.body: A budget alert only sends email. Until the query changes or a quota stops it, the dashboard spends about $1,200 a day.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Start with Cloud Billing reports grouped by project, service and SKU: the increase is BigQuery Analysis in mkt-analytics since last Tuesday. The job history shows the new sales dashboard scanning about 2 TiB every 15 minutes because the table is not partitioned, about $50 an hour at $6.25 per TiB. The project's labels name its owner; cost management is shared, with the owner accountable for the workload, so their team partitions the table and refreshes hourly over 7 days, well before Sales' 14:00 review. The existing budget was alerts-only and never capped spending, so add a 50 TiB daily query quota, a project budget that alerts the owner, required team and owner labels, and a monthly cost review. Disabling billing would stop every service in the project.
